findings.evidence: grep -q Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG
findings.note: The pattern and email are unquoted, so the shell parses `Claude`, `Opus`, `5` as extra filename arguments and `<noreply@anthropic.com>` as an input redirection from a nonexistent file, making the command error out rather than genuinely check the commit message.

findings.note: The compose-then-pipe steps are concrete and self-contained, though the claim that '-m' would collapse blank lines while '-F' does not is dubious since both go through the same message-cleanup path and doesn't affect whether the steps themselves are executable.

The working directory is the root of the skill-forge repository and there

findings.evidence:
Git writes the message of the commit it just made to `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG`,
  so this reads back your own commit.
findings.note: COMMIT_EDITMSG is written before commit-msg/pre-commit hooks run and is not reverted if the commit is rejected (or if there's nothing to commit), so grep can exit 0 even though step 2's git commit never actually created a commit.
